references.text: Jesus was on his way up to Jerusalem, which confirms that he was near the city when he told this parable. [ref:Luk 19:28|Luke 19:28]
Jesus had already told the disciples that they were on their way up to Jerusalem, where he would suffer and die. [ref:Luk 18:31-33|Luke 18:31-33]

The Pharisees asked when the kingdom of God was coming. Jesus answered that the kingdom of God does not come in a way that can be seen with the eyes—it is already among you. This corrects the expectation of an immediate, visible kingdom. [ref:Luk 17:20-21|Luke 17:20-21]
The travelers to Emmaus expressed disappointment that they had hoped Jesus was the one who would redeem Israel—they had expected an immediate messianic kingdom. [ref:Luk 24:21|Luke 24:21]
Even after the resurrection, the disciples ask if Jesus will now restore the kingdom for Israel. The expectation of an immediate kingdom of God persisted. [ref:Apg 1:6-7|Acts 1:6-7]

The parable of the talents in Matthew has a similar structure: a master who goes away, entrusts his servants with money, and expects a return upon his coming back. [ref:Matt 25:14-15|Matthew 25:14-15]

In the parable of the talents, the master returns after a long time to settle accounts, just as the king in Luke 19 does. This emphasizes that the kingdom of God does not come immediately. [ref:Matt 25:19|Matthew 25:19]

The parable Jesus told is about a man of noble birth who went to a distant country to be appointed king—an indirect description that there would be time before the kingdom was established. [ref:Luk 19:12|Luke 19:12]

Jesus says that when you see all these things happening, you should know that the kingdom of God is near. The kingdom would thus not be revealed immediately, but after certain signs. [ref:Luk 21:31|Luke 21:31]
Daniel's vision of the Son of Man receiving kingdom and power from the Ancient of Days points to a future messianic kingdom, not one that comes immediately. [ref:Dan 7:13-14|Daniel 7:13-14]
The crowd followed Jesus because they expected the kingdom of God, and Jesus spoke to them about the kingdom of God. [ref:Luk 9:11|Luke 9:11]
